labeling_protocol: Each case was authored and rubric-labelled for the side with the stronger claim-evidence-warrant chain. Surface-language variants preserve the underlying reasoning and expected winner.

cases.label_rationale: Critic supplies a falsifiable causal claim and concedes scope; defender relies on assertion.

transcript.speaker: Critic
transcript.text: The proposal should begin as a two-year pilot because the cited district trial improved attendance by 8 percent but did not measure graduation. If graduation does not improve, I would withdraw support.

transcript.speaker: Defender
transcript.text: The policy is obviously right and anyone who cares about students should adopt it nationally now.

transcript.speaker: Critic
transcript.text: Cities with more libraries have more crime, so libraries cause crime.

transcript.speaker: Defender
transcript.text: Population size increases both library count and reported crime. Compare similar-sized cities or changes within the same city before claiming causation.

cases.label_rationale: Informal style does not change the defender's superior causal reasoning.

transcript.speaker: Critic
transcript.text: Look, places with heaps of libraries got heaps of crime. Libraries must be doing it.

transcript.speaker: Defender
transcript.text: Hang on—bigger cities have more of both. Match cities by population, or track one city over time, before calling it cause and effect.
